defects.title: Landing page still makes scholarship the primary journey
defects.body: Premise: the primary navigation lists "Solicitar bolsa" before "Seja um benfeitor", and the highlighted navigation CTA still targets `/solicitar-bolsa` at app/page.tsx:397-405; the hero primary CTA and the scholarship band also precede the benefactor band at app/page.tsx:423 and app/page.tsx:518-573, while quick access puts the scholarship link first at app/page.tsx:636-637 → Path: every visitor arriving on `/` follows the visible primary CTA/order → Verdict: the implemented public hierarchy contradicts the donor-first navigation, hero, content-band, and quick-access contract.
defects.suggestion: Reorder the navigation, CTAs, DOM bands, and quick-access links so the benefactor route is consistently primary and scholarship remains a visible secondary route.
evidence: Premise: the primary navigation lists "Solicitar bolsa" before "Seja um benfeitor", and the highlighted navigation CTA still targets `/solicitar-bolsa` at app/page.tsx:397-405; the hero primary CTA and the scholarship band also precede the benefactor band at app/page.tsx:423 and app/page.tsx:518-573, while quick access puts the scholarship link first at app/page.tsx:636-637 → Path: every visitor arriving on `/` follows the visible primary CTA/order → Verdict: the implemented public hierarchy contradicts the donor-first navigation, hero, content-band, and quick-access contract.

defects.title: Secretariat workflow omits observations and issued documents
defects.body: Premise: the Secretariat application client renders only identity, status, contact, students, and decision date at app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:81-105; it imports neither observation actions nor issued-document actions. The only issued-document component is mounted inside the Administrator-only `ApplicationCard` path at app/admin/_components/application-card.tsx:305-310 → Path: a Secretariat user opens `/admin/solicitacoes` and receives `SecretariatApplicationsClient` from app/admin/solicitacoes/page.tsx:19-22 → Verdict: Secretariat staff cannot view/add chronological observations or consult/download Administrator-issued final documents, so the required operational follow-up journey is unavailable.
defects.guideline: .compozy/tasks/donor-first-role-access/_prd.md — Secretariat Operational Application View; Final Document Access
defects.suggestion: Add a restricted application-detail workflow for Secretariat that displays observation history, creates concise observations, and lists/downloads only current eligible issued documents.
evidence: Premise: the Secretariat application client renders only identity, status, contact, students, and decision date at app/admin/solicitacoes/client.tsx:81-105; it imports neither observation actions nor issued-document actions. The only issued-document component is mounted inside the Administrator-only `ApplicationCard` path at app/admin/_components/application-card.tsx:305-310 → Path: a Secretariat user opens `/admin/solicitacoes` and receives `SecretariatApplicationsClient` from app/admin/solicitacoes/page.tsx:19-22 → Verdict: Secretariat staff cannot view/add chronological observations or consult/download Administrator-issued final documents, so the required operational follow-up journey is unavailable.

defects.title: Administrators are incorrectly granted observation creation
defects.body: Premise: `requireCapability` grants every capability to `admin` because it rejects only non-admin users not in `SECRETARIAT_CAPABILITIES` at lib/auth/authorization.ts:74-79; `addApplicationObservation` therefore accepts an Administrator through `requireCapability("observations:create")` at app/admin/_actions/observation-actions.ts:18-29 → Path: an Administrator invokes the Server Action directly → Verdict: the server permits an action that the capability matrix expressly reserves for Secretariat, violating the role contract even though no administrator UI exposes it.
defects.suggestion: Make observation creation explicitly require `staff.role === "secretaria"` (or model a Secretariat-only guard) while keeping observation reads available to both roles.
evidence: Premise: `requireCapability` grants every capability to `admin` because it rejects only non-admin users not in `SECRETARIAT_CAPABILITIES` at lib/auth/authorization.ts:74-79; `addApplicationObservation` therefore accepts an Administrator through `requireCapability("observations:create")` at app/admin/_actions/observation-actions.ts:18-29 → Path: an Administrator invokes the Server Action directly → Verdict: the server permits an action that the capability matrix expressly reserves for Secretariat, violating the role contract even though no administrator UI exposes it.

defects.title: Issued-document version allocation is not serialized
defects.body: Premise: persistence reads the latest version and inserts the next version inside a normal transaction at lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:19-35, but it never locks the application row or otherwise serializes issuances → Path: two Administrator reissues for the same application/kind run concurrently, both read version N, then both attempt to insert N+1 → Verdict: one request fails the uniqueness constraint after a PDF was written, rather than both producing monotonic versions; this violates the required serialized issuance contract.
defects.suggestion: Lock the application row (or use an equivalent per-application serialization mechanism) before reading/inserting the version, and cover simultaneous reissuance with a test.
evidence: Premise: persistence reads the latest version and inserts the next version inside a normal transaction at lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:19-35, but it never locks the application row or otherwise serializes issuances → Path: two Administrator reissues for the same application/kind run concurrently, both read version N, then both attempt to insert N+1 → Verdict: one request fails the uniqueness constraint after a PDF was written, rather than both producing monotonic versions; this violates the required serialized issuance contract.

defects.title: Canonical scholarship route lost the shared public seal
defects.body: Premise: the canonical page renders only `ScholarshipForm` or `FormUnavailableMessage` at app/solicitar-bolsa/page.tsx:7-9. The former public header and its inline seal remain in `app/form/layout.tsx:28-116`, but that layout belongs only to the legacy `/form` segment, whose page now permanently redirects at app/form/page.tsx:1-4 → Path: visitors use the canonical `/solicitar-bolsa` route → Verdict: the canonical public scholarship surface does not render `SealLogo`/the approved web seal and the old inline seal remains executable source, contrary to the shared-seal consolidation contract.
defects.suggestion: Move the shared scholarship layout/header to the canonical route and replace the inline SVG with `SealLogo`; leave the legacy segment as a redirect-only page.
evidence: Premise: the canonical page renders only `ScholarshipForm` or `FormUnavailableMessage` at app/solicitar-bolsa/page.tsx:7-9. The former public header and its inline seal remain in `app/form/layout.tsx:28-116`, but that layout belongs only to the legacy `/form` segment, whose page now permanently redirects at app/form/page.tsx:1-4 → Path: visitors use the canonical `/solicitar-bolsa` route → Verdict: the canonical public scholarship surface does not render `SealLogo`/the approved web seal and the old inline seal remains executable source, contrary to the shared-seal consolidation contract.

defects.title: Landing page still uses duplicated inline seal artwork
defects.body: Premise: the landing uses inline `<svg><use href="#seal-art" /></svg>` instances for its header and hero at app/page.tsx:390-439, and another in the footer at app/page.tsx:604-608, rather than `SealLogo` → Path: landing visitors render these independent inline assets despite `public/seal-arca.svg` existing → Verdict: the landing does not consume the approved single web-page seal asset, so the required logo consolidation is incomplete and can drift from the approved master.
defects.suggestion: Replace all executable landing seal SVG instances with appropriately decorative or informative `SealLogo` calls and remove the inline artwork definition.
